newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan chip giants to boost 64-megabit DRAM output.
newsitem.headline: Japan chip giants to boost 64-megabit DRAM output.

text.p: A group of five Japanese computer chip giants will boost by tenfold production of next-generation 64-megabit Dynamic Random Access Memory (DRAM) chips, a Japanese business daily reported on Friday.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported that NEC Corp., Toshiba Corp, Hitachi Ltd., Fujitsu Ltd and Mitsubishi Electric Corp will increase combined output of 64-megabit DRAM semiconductors to 7.5 million units by the end of 1997, from 700,000 at the end of 1996.

NEC will increase its output from the current 500,000 to 3 million units by switching facilities in Hiroshima and Scotland intended for 16-megabit DRAM chip manufacture over to 64-megabit DRAM production.
"We'll consider upping production to 5 million units if there is demand," the daily quoted a company source as saying.

All five companies are cutting back on current mainstay 16-megabit DRAM development, the Nihon Keizai reported, adding that the companies together hold a 40 percent share of the world DRAM semiconductors market.

The business daily quoted market sources as saying 64-megabit DRAM chips will cost on average 65,000 yen in January, down from 90,000 yen a year ago and a steeper price fall than the 16-megabit DRAM chip which is now a fifth of its original price.

The price of 64-megabit DRAM chips will fall from ten times to around four times that of 16-megabit DRAM chips by mid-1997, ushering in a new generation of faster, smaller personal computers and miniaturised media devices almost a year and a half earlier than had been expected, the business daily reported.
